meta.title: Before AI: 2015, three sprites live · Fizlet
meta.description: Three CSS sprite animations Chris Cooley drew by hand in 2015, live beside a Fizlet remake and an arcade version, taken apart with bricks and sizes.

main:
Fizlet / Notes / Before AI: 2015 / The three, live

2015 BEFORE AI · THE INTERACTIVE COMPANION

Drawn by hand in 2015.
Rebuilt in Fizlet.

In 2015, years before AI coding tools, Chris Cooley drew three micro animations frame by frame and played them with CSS sprites: headphones that plug in and play, a coffee cup that fills, a laptop that opens and types. The Wayback Machine kept them. Here they are live, beside the same three on Fizlet: once as they were, once as an arcade.

By Chris Cooley ↗ · Read the note: Before AI: 2015

ON THIS PAGE
  1. 01Three ways
  2. 02One comparison
  3. 03Taken apart
  4. 04The archive
  • 1,870 B

    2015, gzip: the CSS and the 4-line toggle. Bricks: none

  • 4,912 B

    the remake, gzip: JS (the kernel and the strip that plays the frames) and CSS

  • 12,402 B

    the arcade, gzip: JS (kernel, @fzlt/core/fx, @fzlt/core/sound, @fzlt/core/hud) and CSS

  • 0

    animation frames a second the arcade asks for once a round is over

01 THREE WAYS · LIVE

Same sprite sheets.
×100 the life.

Press the switches in the first two columns. In the arcade, hit everything: the headphones, the cup, the keys.

  1. 2015

    01 THE ORIGINAL

    2015 · CSS sprites

    Oh, that's cool.

    • no bricks
    • CSS + 4 lines 1,870 B

    The 2015 CSS, byte for byte, and the 4-line class toggle that stood in for Angular's ng-click. The headphone switch is a div, as it was: mouse only.

  2. REMAKE

    02 THE REMAKE

    Fizlet · remake

    Same thing. Rebuilt in minutes.

    • @fzlt/core 3,372 B

    Same frames, timings and clicks, rebuilt in about 6 minutes of agent time (container clock). The kernel owns the clock instead of @keyframes, and sleeps when nothing moves.

  3. ×100

    03 THE ARCADE

    Fizlet · arcade

    Now hit it. ×100.

    • @fzlt/core 3,372 B
    • @fzlt/core/fx 2,792 B
    • @fzlt/core/sound 1,062 B
    • @fzlt/core/hud 1,306 B
    Score 0Combo ×0Best ×0

    The same 2015 frames. Hit the cups: bass, bounce, notes, an equalizer on the phone. Pour and sip: splash, steam, slurp. Open the lid, then hammer the keys: clicks, code spray, a lit screen. Hit fast to chain the combo.

Reduced motion: the 2015 column and the remake hold their first frame (a wrapper rule on this page; 2015 had none), and the arcade lands each press on its still frame with no particles, squash or shake; it makes a sound only when you press, and the Sound key mutes it. At rest the page asks for no animation frames, even after a round in the arcade; the site's tests count them on every build. On the page both Fizlet columns ship as one script, 14,218 B gzip (they share the kernel), plus 1,425 B of CSS. The sprite sheets are the same files in all three.

Give the page back: every engine stops and every style, class and attribute Fizlet wrote goes back as it was. Press either Fizlet column to start it again.

03 HOW EACH ONE MOVES

Taken apart.
Every byte counted.

2015

01 THE ORIGINAL

2015 · CSS sprites

Bricks: none. CSS and 4 lines.

The process: draw every frame by hand, lay the frames side by side on one long sheet, then show the sheet through a box one frame wide. @keyframes slide background-position from the first frame to the last, and steps(n) makes it jump frame to frame instead of gliding. A click toggles one class, which swaps the animation.

The 2015 toggle, all 4 lines
document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
  var sw = e.target.closest('[data-toggle]');
  if (sw) sw.parentNode.classList.toggle(sw.getAttribute('data-toggle'));
});
REMAKE

02 THE REMAKE

Fizlet · remake

Bricks: the kernel. Nothing else.

  • @fzlt/core 3,372 B

The @keyframes become data: each segment is a first frame, a last frame, the jumps and the seconds, read by one engine per sprite. beatsPlug 1.4s steps(13) is { a: 0, b: 13, n: 13, d: 1.4 }. The kernel owns the clock, writes background-position through the ledger only when the frame changes, and sleeps when nothing plays.

// strip.ts: the frame at time t, exactly steps(n), jump-end
a + floor((t - w) / d * n) / n * (b - a)

Like 2015, the laptop's code scrolls forever once it is open, so the remake keeps asking for frames while it does. That is the fair copy.

×100

03 THE ARCADE

Fizlet · arcade

Bricks: kernel, @fzlt/core/fx, @fzlt/core/sound, @fzlt/core/hud.

    • @fzlt/core 3,372 B
    the clock, settle, the ledger
    • @fzlt/core/fx 2,792 B
    notes, code, splash, steam, combo words
    • @fzlt/core/sound 1,062 B
    thump, clack, keys, pour, slurp: a synth, no files
    • @fzlt/core/hud 1,306 B
    score, combo, best: change-only writes

The art is the 2015 frames, untouched. Squash, wobble and the stage shake are one style each, written through the ledger and given back when they stop. The particles draw on one canvas per sprite, only while one is alive. Each sprite's engine and the column's own (HUD, combo, shake) settle on their own, so after the last spark the page asks for nothing.

Measured on this build (site/demos/before-ai-2015/build.mjs): a brick's size is the whole brick, minified and gzipped with everything it pulls in, as npm run size measures it; a column's size is that column alone, bundled and gzipped the way this page's script is, so it counts only the parts of each brick it uses. Sheet and font sizes are the files on disk. The 0 at rest is counted by tests/site.mjs in Chromium on every build.

04 THE ARCHIVE

The 2015 page.
Still on the archive.

meta.title: Fizz: crack the can, hear the fizz · Fizlet
meta.description: An arcade soda can crunches, pops and sprays fizz out of its card, seen from the side and from the top. 8665 B gzip live chunk, by Chris Cooley.

main:
Fizlet / The name / The fizz proof piece

FZ THE NAME · A PROOF PIECE

Crack the can.
Hear the fizz.

The soda-ad shot. Tap the can: it crunches, the tab pops, and the fizz sprays clean out of the card. Two views tell it side by side: the can from the side, and straight down into it as it fizzes.

By Chris Cooley ↗.

-let, as in applet: a very small app with one job. Fiz-, from the old soda commercial: a can cracks, the shot zooms in on the bubbles and the drip running down the side.

That shot looks expensive. Up close the fizz is full of detail, the kind of thing you'd reach for a heavy animation library to make. You don't need much to make it, though. That's the whole point: motion that looks complex, a tiny footprint, and the page as the stage.

It started with DOM VIRUS: small games with a few characters, running right inside a page, changing the DOM itself and then giving it back. The bar for every brick since is simple: do one thing well, and fit with everything around it.

LIVE · TAP THE CAN

Live chunk 8,665 B gzip (kernel + fx + sprite + the can, both views) · loader 2,040 B (@fzlt/core/slot) · poster 3,457 B · script per frame at 4× CPU throttle 1.1 ms avg, 13.6 ms max · settled: 0 frames a second. Measured in Chromium 153, 2026-10-30.

Kernel

settle and fps: 30. It runs while something moves, then sleeps: no frames at all until a tap.

@fzlt/core/fx

Two fixed pools. The spray flies on a layer above the card, so nothing crops it; the top view fizzes inside. Geyser, burst, bubbles, rings: kinds as data, sprayed with emit().

@fzlt/core/sprite

The can is pixel data: 20 × 40 from the side, 22 × 22 from the top, crunched or not. Baked once; the poster is the same pixels as SVG.

@fzlt/core/slot

Loads near the viewport, on an idle main thread. Reduced motion keeps the still frame; the scene never loads.

html:
Layers

A game is a stack.
Each layer, one brick.

Battlefield Blitz turns sideways and lifts apart into its layers, one at a time, each labelled with the bytes its own code costs. One layer faults, a scan patches it, and the stack snaps back into the game. It plays on its own; the play key pauses it. Scroll or swipe over it to fan the layers by hand (it holds the page while you do, like every demo here), or focus it and step through with the arrow keys.

7.8 KB gz

Live chunk 7.9 KB gzip (slot + scene, one file), loaded only once the slot is near. Inline poster and loader 4.0 KB. At 4× CPU throttle, script per frame over one loop 1.2 ms median, 3.3 ms p95, capped at 30 fps. Layout shift 0. Paused: 0 frames. Measured in Chromium 153 on Fizlet 0.21.1.

Layer bytes: Battlefield Blitz c8c8ca4, layer manifest (game code per layer, min + gzip; Effects is all brick, min). Built on @fzlt/core, @fzlt/core/slot and @fzlt/core/sprite. By Chris Cooley ↗.

meta.title: Fizlet → fzlt: the name shift · Fizlet
meta.description: The launch logo: FIZ and LET go into a press and come out as fzlt, then build a wall of bricks. 5,726 B gzip live, still once it ends. By Chris Cooley.

main:
Fizlet / Daily / Fizlet → fzlt

FZ THE NAME SHIFT · A HERO SCENE

Fizlet → fzlt

Fizlet is the name; fzlt is the short mark. Two keys, FIZ and LET, go into the press. The E and the I drop out, and fzlt comes out. The press stacks it on a wall of bricks, and it ends on the lockup. It plays once when it comes into view, then the page is still (no frames); the Replay key plays it again. With reduced motion you see the last frame, still. By Chris Cooley ↗.

5.6 KB gz Live chunk 5,726 B gzip (kernel + @fzlt/core/timeline + the scene) · loader 2,239 B (@fzlt/core/slot) · total 7,965 B. Measured on this build.

Embed it in any slot: its figure (figure() in site/gallery/pieces/name-shift/art.ts) and one line:

slot(figure, () => import("/gallery/fizlet-to-fzlt.js").then((m) => m.mount))

meta.title: Origin: Code. Sleep. Drink. Repeat. · Fizlet
meta.description: A day as a loop: sleep, sunrise, headphones, coffee, code, night. The 2015 props alive in 35,611 B gzip. By Chris Cooley.

main:
Fizlet / Daily / Origin

OG THE ORIGIN · A HERO SCENE

. Sleep. Drink. Repeat.

A designer's and developer's day as a loop. Night: head down on the desk. The sun comes up, the headphones go on, the coffee goes down, and the laptop and phone run all day. Night falls, the lid closes, repeat. Tap the word to switch the screens between code and design work. Close the laptop and he sleeps; open it and the day starts.

Why Fizlet. There were a lot of animations before Fizlet, and in between. We kept writing the same thing over and over, a little different each time for a slightly different use. So we built Fizlet to make it easier for us. Then we figured other people could get something out of it too, so we open-sourced it.

Inspired by the original 2015 portfolio, with Fizlet flair. The headphones, the coffee and the laptop are the props from my 2015 portfolio, back as living things; in the 2015 look the cup is the 2015 sprite sheet itself. The look key switches between the 2015 palette and Fizlet's: cyberpunk meets Tron, in the site's own tokens. By Chris Cooley ↗.

The cup is a toy. Tap it for a sip, double-tap it to refill it, drag it anywhere on the desk, flick it to knock it over (tap the spill, or wait). On the keyboard: Enter sips, R refills, the arrow keys move it.

Tap the plant to water it, the notebook and he writes a line of code or draws a doodle, the lamp to switch the light. Tap the phone for country, rock or pop: each a one-bar loop on the audio clock; a double-tap pauses it. Tap the laptop's screen and he sleeps; tap it again and he wakes. Keep feeding him coffee and he won't sleep. The scene keeps its own day: light by day, dark by night.

Live chunk 35,611 B gzip (six bricks + the scene) · loader 2,128 B (@fzlt/core/slot) · poster 6,556 B inline (both looks) · 2015 coffee sheet 6,961 B PNG. Measured on this build.

meta.title: Quick start: ten lines to a blast · Fizlet
meta.description: Ten lines to a blast: the Fizlet quick start, running as is. Click the board; scroll it away and the engine pauses, switch tabs and it stops.

main:
Fizlet / Quick start / The example, running

EX QUICK START · RUNNING

Ten lines
to a blast.

This page runs the snippet below, as is. Click the board. Scroll it away and the engine pauses; switch tabs and it stops.

13.5 KB gz LIVE · CLICK THE BOARD TO BLAST
SOURCE · the whole thing
<canvas id="board" width="640" height="320"></canvas>
<script src="https://fizlet.com/fizlet.js"></script>
<script>
  const { createEngine, effects } = fizlet;
  const canvas = document.getElementById("board"), ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
  const engine = createEngine({ root: canvas }), fx = effects();
  canvas.onclick = (ev) => fx.blast(ev.offsetX * 640 / canvas.clientWidth, ev.offsetY * 320 / canvas.clientHeight);
  engine.add({
    step: (e, dt) => fx.step(dt),
    render: () => (ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 640, 320), fx.drawGround(ctx), fx.draw(ctx)),
  });
  engine.start();
</script>
